title: Mean square of a matching Fourier factor
statement: Let $q,k,n$ be natural numbers with $n>0$, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and let a perfect matching of the complete $q$-partite graph with $k$ vertices in each part be given, together with a part of that graph. Assign each matching edge independently and uniformly a label from $\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$. For each assignment, take the absolute value of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ indexed by the set of labels on the matching edges incident with the specified part. The expected square of this quantity equals the expected square of the Fourier coefficient indexed by the set of values of a uniformly random map from $\\{1,\\ldots,k\\}$ to $\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
A perfect matching in the stated complete multipartite graph is given
A part of the graph is specified
